note: The non-palette-card assets that still carry unusually high reuse value: the tool UI for authoring colour, music-player component detail, and the still-frame before/after comparisons. Each was read at native resolution.

items.title: Add New Element — animation authoring panel
items.description: A phone screen from a design-tool app titled 'Add New Element', presenting a dense vertical form. Fields run down in a single column: Element Name, Element Type (a dropdown reading 'Function'), Start Time (ms) and Duration (ms) with numeric steppers, Function Type set to 'Linear', then Origin Y/X, Scale, Opacity and a Color field showing the hex value '#FF03A8F4' as inline coloured text. The whole panel is white with hairline dashed row separators and small right-aligned chevrons. Worth studying because it is the opposite of the usual minimal mobile screen: everything is visible, nothing is hidden behind progressive disclosure, and it stays readable because the row rhythm is absolutely consistent and the type sizes are locked to two values.
items.quality: Clear capture; hex value and field labels legible.

items.title: Music player with waveform scrubber
items.description: A media-player surface on a vivid violet-to-magenta gradient. A white rounded card floats in the centre carrying an audio scrubber: a waveform in pink, a time readout '0:15 / 0:60', a circular play button, and a tick-marked timeline ruled in 0.05 increments from 0.00 to 0.40. Below sits a row of album artwork thumbnails with a pink 'Free Bird · Lynyrd Skynyrd' label and an add button. The design demonstrates a strong technique: rather than one progress bar, three levels of time information coexist — elapsed, remaining, and a fine-grained ruler. The gradient behind is doing the work of setting energy so the card can stay completely plain white.
items.quality: Good capture. Scrubber detail is legible at native resolution.

items.title: Cinematic character-and-creature composition
items.description: A wide, dark, high-contrast illustration: a figure in a black jacket mid-strike with a luminous purple blade, confronting a large biomechanical creature against a desaturated grey environment. Cinematic lighting, strong rim light on both subjects, heavy atmospheric haze. Retained as a reference for tonal depth and focal separation rather than for interface work — the technique worth stealing is that the brightest saturated element in a near-monochrome scene becomes the focal point instantly, which is the same principle as an accent colour on a dark UI.
items.quality: High-resolution image, not a UI capture. Filed as illustration reference.
items.source_note: AI-generated artwork present in the collection. Kept for the lighting lesson, not as design provenance.

items.title: Light vs dark document theme (still frame)
items.description: Two document pages presented side by side. The left is a pale sage-cream page with dense small text and a brick-red bookmark strip down the right edge; the right is the same document in a dark theme with white body text, a highlighted heading, and the bookmark strip retained. Both keep identical measure and type sizing, which is the right call: changing the column width between themes would make the dark version feel like a different document rather than the same one at night.
items.quality: Text too small to read at this size; the layout and theme delta are what is legible.

items.title: Nepali-language app menu screen
items.description: A portrait phone screen with a DejaVu-style Devanagari heading ('फेन्द्री') and a list of detailed service rows, each with small-print descriptions beneath the label. A horizontally scrolling tab row sits near the top with two segment buttons, one filled solid orange and one outlined, and the list below shows paired label/value rows. Notable because it is one of the few genuinely localised interfaces in the collection — the type is set for Devanagari rather than a Latin face with localised text dropped in, and the row heights have been increased to accommodate the taller script.
items.quality: Readable at native resolution; the small-print descriptions are borderline.
items.source_note: Localised Nepali interface. Useful as evidence for how line-height must change with script.

items.title: Money-tracking store panel — $48.60 total card
items.description: An App Store style panel: a phone mockup on a light grey field showing a finance screen. A white card dominates with a large '$48.60' total, small category chips beneath ('Groceries', 'Transport', 'Food'), and a segmented All/In/Out row. Below the card, three module tiles appear — one pink, one green, one neutral — each carrying a small icon and label, before a recent-transactions list. The composition is the standard store-panel formula: one hero figure, three supporting modules, list preview at the fold, with enough white space that the phone reads as an object rather than a window.
items.quality: Clean store capture at native resolution.

items.title: Spending app store panel — $55 category card
items.description: A store panel pairing. The primary phone shows a rounded card settled on a warm yellow field with a large '$55' figure, a small star rating, and two pill buttons; behind it a second phone shows a 'More Pages' grid of colourful module tiles (pink, blue, green, orange) each carrying an icon and label. Strong example of the module-grid home screen: instead of a feed, the app is a set of destinations, which works when the product's value is a collection of discrete tools rather than a stream.

items.title: Payments app store panel — $24 transfer card
items.description: Two overlapping phone mockups on white. The nearer screen shows a transfer summary centred on a single '$24' figure with a purple 'Send' button below and a light summary row; the further screen shows an activity list with colour-coded entries. The layout makes a clear choice: the amount is the screen, with everything else — recipient, note, method — demoted to small muted rows. That is the correct hierarchy for a payment confirmation, where the user's only question is 'is the number right'.
